summary: Morgan James, a woman who has been held and is being used for reproductive purposes, calls the owner's son at a clinic-like facility asking whether Steve Abrams is staying there, and learns no one by that name is there. Her call to the embassy is delayed until morning, so she turns to the facility's computers, where she is unsettled by a file listing and a list of six women's names marked "terminated." The name M. James appears at the bottom of the list, though she has not been terminated yet. The passage is a suspenseful excerpt from a novel labeled Book 3, part 158.
one_line: Morgan James phones the facility for Steve Abrams, then finds a file on the computers listing six women, including herself, marked "terminated."
key_facts: Morgan James calls the facility at an early hour and asks for Steve Abrams, and the owner's son replies that nobody by that name stays there.
The owner's son is described as trying his best to learn English and greets her with "Hey, que pasa, Senora James."
Morgan James decides not to call the embassy yet because she does not want to use up her opening shot with the graveyard shift.
She hopes that by 6 A.M. somebody with authority to do something will be at the embassy.
Morgan James is a Mac fan who hates Windows and must proceed by trial and error on the terminal.
She finds an index of files that includes a long list of names, along with plant-extract categories and scientific terms.
Morgan James finds a file named QUETZAL containing a short list of six women's names, organized by dates about a year apart.
Each of the six women listed in the QUETZAL file is indicated as "terminated" at the end.
The name next to the last entry is S. Crenshaw, who is also marked "terminated."
The bottom of the QUETZAL list is M. James, but Morgan James notes that she has not been "terminated." Not yet.
Morgan James first assumes the women were patients from Quetzal Manor who came for fertility treatment.
Morgan James wonders what Steve Abrams's research on the local flora requires her ova for.
